---
title: "Fisheries Decision Making"
---

## Overview

Modern fisheries management requires tools that can explicitly account for environmental changes and observational uncertainties. This initiative evaluates how climate risks and data limitations impact harvest control rules (HCRs) and Acceptable Biological Catch (ABC) advice, supporting regional councils as they modernize risk policies and operationalize climate-informed management. The Fisheries Decision Making team conducts simulation testing on the performance of fisheries management strategies in the face of escalating climate impacts and data uncertainties. By utilizing and expanding Management Strategy Evaluation (MSE) frameworks, this project bridges climate science and fisheries management to support setting robust catch advice.

::: callout-note
### Key Objective

Explore approaches to account for climate risk in setting catch advice.
:::

### Current Initiatives

-   **Framework Development:** Leveraging existing models like Groundfish-MSE.
-   **Stakeholder Integration:** Aligning ecosystem trade-offs with community and management priorities.
-   **Climate-Informed Catch Advice:** Establishing frameworks to set Acceptable Biological Catch (ABC) while accounting for changing ecosystem productivity.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
